First listed 2025-08-08 · episode or wrap

Tariffs Are Back, Apple’s Big Bet, and AI’s Real Impact - The Friday Market Wrap!

Eisman distinguishes headline tariffs from effective rates, questions Apple spending promises, and surveys AI beneficiaries and potential victims. Gartner is his early example of AI threatening an incumbent information business. The wrap also contrasts current biotech earnings with pipeline news and reiterates skepticism about Opendoor.

YouTube · 2025-08-08 ↗Substack · 2025-08-08 ↗
The most consequential uncertainty is causal: Gartner weakness does not yet prove free AI substitution. Apple skepticism uses an inconsistent spending comparison because its US commitment includes suppliers, employees and content as well as physical investment. The pipeline discussion is useful if clinical outcomes are separated from investor expectations.

How he reasons here

  • Calculate effective policy exposure after exemptions.
  • Read the definition behind a large investment announcement.
  • Distinguish proprietary economics from commodity hardware.
  • Separate pipeline value from current earnings.
  • Look for both winners and threatened incumbents in AI.

Tools and charts discussed

Mentioned in the transcript; visual charts have not all been inspected.

  • Trade-weighted tariff rates
  • Announced versus incremental domestic spending
  • Government versus commercial revenue
  • Biotech trial endpoints and estimands
  • Revenue guidance versus EPS guidance
  • Industrial order cycles
  • Information-service contract value
